newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Avon to invest extra $50 mln in Brazil in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Avon to invest extra $50 mln in Brazil in 1997.

text.p: Cosmetics manufacturer Avon Products Inc will add an extra $50 million to its planned investment of $112 million in Brazil in 1997, daily newspaper Estado de Sao Paulo said.
"If we had to build new factories, we wouldn't do it in Chile, in Argentina or Mexico," Avon Chairman James Preston told the newspaper in an interview.
"We'll build it here, because Brazil has been and will be our main production and commercialisation base in Latin America," he added.

The extra investment will go towards modernizing technology in order to facilitate the sale and distribution of products in Brazil, said Ademar Serodio, head of Avon's Brazilian subsidiary Avon Cosmeticos Ltda.
Avon shares fell on the New York Stock Exchange on Friday after the company's second quarter results showed a decline in sales and pre-tax profits in Brazil.
This was due to continued softness in consumer spending and the company's ongoing inventory reduction programs, Avon said.
But Preston said he remained confident in Brazil's growth in the long-term.
"I feel encouraged, like never before, by the long-term prospects," he said. "You have to look at Brazil not within the context of a year, but with a broader horizon, of five or 10 years."

Brazil is Avon's largest market after the United States with revenues of $1.2 billion last year. The company employs 520,000 sales staff across the country, who sell products in regions as remote as the Amazon basin.

However, Avon's fastest-growing market is Russia and sales there are forecast to rise to $80 million in 1997 from $45 million the previous year, Preston said. In China, sales are expected to rise to $130 million from $90 million in 1996.
